beginner.headline: Rare Harper Lee Book Found in Oxfam Shop
beginner.brief: A rare book was found in an Oxfam shop in London. It is a first edition of the novel 'To Kill a Mockingbird' by Harper Lee. The book was donated to the charity's bookshop. A shop manager found this special book and knew it was important. The outside cover was old, but the pages inside were in beautiful condition. Now, the book is part of the national collection at the British Library. This discovery reminds people about treasures found in second-hand shops. Oxfam's 'Second Hand September' campaign encourages buying used items.

intermediate.headline: Rare Harper Lee First Edition Found in Oxfam Shop Goes to British Library
intermediate.brief: A first edition of the novel To Kill A Mockingbird has been found among items donated to Oxfam, according to the charity. The copy of Harper Lee's seminal 1960 work was discovered in a box of American books given to a bookshop in west London. It has since been acquired by the British Library and will join its national collection. Shop manager Olivia Haysman-Walker identified the copy as being a first US edition, saying it could easily have been missed. She realised quickly that they had something truly valuable. Although its dust jacket was worn around the edges, the pages inside were in beautiful condition. It is remarkable to think this book passed through the Oxfam bookshop and into the British Library's national collection. This discovery is a lovely reminder, during Second Hand September, of treasures hiding among donations in charity shops. Second Hand September is Oxfam's annual campaign encouraging people to buy second-hand items. Lee's Pulitzer Prize-winning book tells a story of racial injustice and childhood innocence, selling over 40 million copies worldwide.

advanced.headline: Harper Lee First Edition Discovered in Oxfam Donation Joins British Library
advanced.brief: An original US first edition of Harper Lee's renowned novel, "To Kill a Mockingbird," was recently discovered within a donation to an Oxfam charity shop. This significant literary find, the seminal 1960 work, emerged from a box of American books at the charity's Portobello Road bookshop in west London. The valuable copy has since been acquired by the British Library, where it is destined to enrich its extensive national collection. Olivia Haysman-Walker, the shop manager, identified this particular US first edition, noting its potential to have been easily overlooked. She explained that despite the sheer volume of incoming donations, staff recognized the iconic novel and decided to scrutinize it more closely. Oxfam personnel quickly discerned they were in possession of a truly exceptional item, recognizing its profound historical significance. Although its dust jacket bore the marks of age and was somewhat worn around the edges, the internal pages remained in pristine condition. Haysman-Walker expressed her amazement that such a valuable artifact journeyed from their bookshop into the prestigious British Library. She characterized this as 'quite a journey' and a 'lovely reminder' during Second Hand September of the unsuspected treasures lurking in charitable donations. Oxfam's annual Second Hand September initiative actively promotes the environmental and economic benefits of purchasing second-hand items. Lee's Pulitzer Prize-winning book chronicles the lawyer Atticus Finch's valiant defense of Tom Robinson, a Black man wrongly accused of raping a white woman. This profound narrative of societal injustice and childhood innocence, set in 1934 Alabama, has sold over 40 million copies globally and been translated into 40 languages. The celebrated US novelist, a recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom, passed away in 2016 at the venerable age of 89.
